outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,800 to $18,000. Notes: The timeline is 120–300 days and the government cost is $3,800–$18,000, both to approval of the Conditional Use Authorization and the health permit (the entitlement path given by the rules). These figures do not include the ABC Type 47 license process, which is listed as insufficient information. If a CUA is required, expect 6–10 months (180–300 days) from filing to Commission approval including pre-application community meeting, environmental review, 300-foot neighbor notification, hearing scheduling, and a 30-day post-decision appeal period; the nearest comparable Type 47 CUA (414 Columbus Avenue) took 270 days from filing to approval. The CUA application fee was approximately $2,747 in 2023–24, CPI-adjusted to roughly $3,150 in 2026–27, and can rise with construction cost; restaurants may qualify for First Year Free fee waivers. The health permit application is $470 (includes initial inspection) with a $0 annual license fee for 2026–28. Other city fees: business registration $55–$700 (tiered by gross receipts), fictitious business name $60–$120, sign permit (if new exterior signage) $300–$1,500, and fire Place of Assembly permit (if seating 50+) $446. State fees: entity formation $70–$150, certified food safety manager exam $100–$250, RBS training per employee $13–$33, food handler cards $7–$15 each, ASCAP+BMI licenses $600–$5,000/year. The Type 47 license itself, if obtained by transfer, costs $100,000–$450,000 market price plus ABC's transfer fees; that cost and its 90–240-day timeline are not included here because how the license will be obtained is not established. If Planning determines the project is a continuation of the existing Type 47 and no CUA is required, the timeline and cost drop to the health permit and ABC referral (roughly 30–60 days and $500–$1,500 in city fees). The day range is the time to obtain the approvals when they are granted; it is not a time to a denial or a withdrawal.

The Type 47 license itself, if obtained by transfer, costs $100,000–$450,000 market price plus ABC's transfer fees; that cost and its 90–240-day timeline are not included here because how the license will be obtained is not established. If Planning determines the project is a continuation of the existing Type 47 and no CUA is required, the timeline and cost drop to the health permit and ABC referral (roughly 30–60 days and $500–$1,500 in city fees). The day range is the time to obtain the approvals when they are granted; it is not a time to a denial or a withdrawal.
